title: Backup & restore
blurb: Back up files, restore from backup, move to a new computer, start fresh.

remedies.title: Back up my computer
remedies.why: A disk can fail, a laptop can be lost and ransomware can lock files; a backup elsewhere is the only fix for all of them.

steps.text: Turn on OneDrive folder backup (Desktop, Documents, Pictures).
Plug in an external drive and turn on File History (Control Panel › File History) for versions of every file.
Plug in an external drive and turn on Time Machine.
Turn on iCloud Drive Desktop & Documents if you use iCloud.
Keep one copy away from the computer (cloud, or a drive stored elsewhere) and test restoring one file now and then.

remedies.title: Move my files to a new computer
remedies.why: Built-in tools carry files, settings and apps across.

steps.text: Windows 11: Windows Backup on the old PC (signed in with your Microsoft account), then restore during setup of the new one; OneDrive carries your files.
Migration Assistant on both Macs (new Mac during setup), over Wi-Fi or cable, or from a Time Machine backup.
Before wiping the old computer, check you can open important files on the new one.
Sign out of apps with licences (Adobe, Office) on the old computer.

remedies.title: Start fresh: reset the computer
remedies.why: A reset fixes deep problems or prepares the computer for someone else. Back up first.

steps.text: Back up your files and check the backup opens.
Settings › System › Recovery › Reset this PC: Keep my files (fixes Windows) or Remove everything (to give it away).
System Settings › General › Transfer or Reset › Erase All Content and Settings.
Have your Microsoft/Apple account password and Wi-Fi password ready.

remedies.escalate: Work computers: ask IT first; they usually reset them with company tools.

remedies.title: Undo a recent change with System Restore
remedies.why: System Restore takes system settings, drivers and apps back to a restore point; your documents stay.

steps.text: Open System Restore and pick a point from before the problem.
Turn on restore points for drive C: (System Properties › System Protection › Configure) so you have them next time.

remedies.title: Get a file back from Time Machine
remedies.why: Time Machine keeps hourly, daily and weekly copies on the backup drive.

steps.text: Connect the backup drive, open the folder the file was in, then click Time Machine in the menu bar › Browse Time Machine Backups.
Scroll back in time, select the file and click Restore.
Turn on "Show Time Machine in menu bar" if it's not there.
